sections.h2: Which Pasco County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices split the work: the Property Appraiser values the land, the Tax Collector bills and collects, and the Clerk and Comptroller runs the appeals board and records the deed. Knowing which one to call saves a lot of transfers.

The Property Appraiser's homepage counts 335,946 real property parcels, including 206,994 single family parcels, 11,888 condominium units, 11,347 commercial parcels and 3,906 agricultural parcels. It lists 747 square miles of land and 122 of water, 869 in all. Its offices are in Dade City (352-521-4433), Land O' Lakes (813-929-2780) and New Port Richey (727-847-8151).

The Tax Collector lists offices in New Port Richey, Gulf Harbors, Land O'Lakes, Wesley Chapel and Dade City, with a sixth at Suncoast Parkway and SR 52 marked as coming soon. Its tax department answers at 352-521-4338, prompt 3.

  • Pasco County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, taxing districts list, records search.
  • Pasco County Tax Collector: bills, online payment, installment plan, partial payment, delinquent taxes.
  • Pasco County Clerk and Comptroller: Value Adjustment Board petitions and the Official Records.

sections.h2: When are Pasco County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Florida's statewide calendar governs: bills go out in November, the early payment discount runs November through February, and the tax is delinquent on April 1. The Pasco Tax Collector's pages repeat the April 1 delinquency date and add the local penalty details below.

Pasco also offers an installment plan for estimated tax above one hundred dollars. For the 2027 tax year the collector's page says applications are available from November 1, 2026 and must be filed by April 30, 2027, and that no applications are taken from May 1 through October 31. Payments fall in June with a 6 percent discount, September with 4.5 percent, December with 3 percent and March with none. The first payment must arrive by July 31 or you are out of the plan. Each parcel needs its own application, and renewal after that is automatic.

A partial payment application also appears on the collector's menu. State law leaves partial payments before the delinquency date to the tax collector's discretion, so ask the office before sending less than the full bill.

sections.h2: How does a Pasco County homestead exemption work?
sections.html:
You file once with the Property Appraiser by March 1, and the exemption then lowers the taxable value of your primary residence. The Tax Collector's own page says it does not handle homestead filings and sends owners to the appraiser, who takes applications year round but applies the March 1 cutoff.

The appraiser's exemptions menu is organized into six groups: Homestead, Disability, Veterans, Military and First Responders, Agriculture, Parent and Grandparent, and Senior Aged 65 and older. State rules put the base homestead benefit at up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 applying to school taxes and the second $25,000 reaching only value above $50,000 for non-school taxes. Some seniors can qualify for an added exemption if the county has adopted it and income falls under a limit; ask the appraiser whether Pasco has.

A sale or deed ends the capped assessment. Florida's rule is that a change of ownership resets the property to just value on the next January 1, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses. The state's 2026 Save Our Homes cap is printed at 2.7 percent.

  • File by March 1 for the year you want the benefit; the home must be your permanent residence on January 1.
  • Renting the home or moving out ends eligibility.
  • A servicemember may rent out the homestead without losing it, under state law.

sections.h2: What happens if Pasco County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The bill becomes delinquent on April 1 with a late penalty, then a lien is sold, and after two years the property can go to public auction. The Pasco Tax Collector's delinquent page gives each step.

It states a late penalty of 3 percent of the tax amount added on April 1, followed by advertising charges. On or before June 1 a tax certificate, a lien against the property, is issued for the unpaid tax, penalties and costs. Interest on the certificate runs from a minimum of 5 percent to a maximum of 18 percent. If the taxes remain unpaid after two years, the property may be sold at public auction.

The collector asks that delinquent payments come by money order, cashier's check or wire, with cash taken in offices only. Personal and business checks are returned, which can add interest. Attorney, title company and mortgage broker escrow checks are accepted.

State law also bars a certificate buyer from contacting you to demand payment for two years after April 1 of the year the certificate was issued, so an early call from a stranger about your lien is a red flag.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when I sell a house in Pasco County?
sections.html:
The title company pays what is owed on the parcel from your sale proceeds, so you do not hand cash to the tax collector yourself. Open or delinquent bills are cleared before the buyer takes title.

The Tax Collector's page on recent purchases explains the follow-up: the Property Appraiser notifies it of ownership changes during the year, and if the taxes are unpaid a duplicate notice is mailed to the new owner. If they are delinquent, a reminder goes to the new owner too. The page also notes that the owner shown on the website is the owner as assessed on the certified tax roll, which is usually finished in early October.

Florida's deed tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in all counties except Miami-Dade, and every party to the deed is liable for it regardless of who agrees to pay. Pasco's clerk charges $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each added page to record, which matches the state statute's base charge plus its added fees.

The buyer's side changes too. Because a sale resets assessed value, the new owner's bill can be well above the seller's capped bill. A buyer who plans to live there should file for homestead by March 1 of the following year.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Pasco County assessment?
sections.html:
Talk to the Property Appraiser first, then file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board through the Pasco Clerk and Comptroller if you still disagree. Board petitions carry a non-refundable $50.00 filing fee under the clerk's FAQ.

The clerk lists two exceptions: a portability petition on the DR-486PORT form costs $15.00, and a petition over a denied homestead application, deployed military exemption or tax deferral has no fee. State law gives 25 days from the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes for a value petition, and 30 days after a denial letter is mailed for an exemption denial. The TRIM notice is mailed in August, so read the dates printed on it.

The tangible personal property return for business equipment and rental furnishings is due April 1. If you rent the house out before selling, ask the appraiser whether a return applies.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Pasco County?
faqs.a: The Pasco County Tax Collector collects it, through five working offices and an online portal. Tax questions go to 352-521-4338, prompt 3. The Property Appraiser sets value and exemptions but takes no payments.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Pasco County property tax?
faqs.a: The Tax Collector's page says a 3 percent late penalty is added on April 1, followed by advertising charges. A tax certificate is issued on or before June 1, carrying interest between 5 percent and 18 percent.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pasco County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, if the estimated tax is over one hundred dollars. Applications for the 2027 tax year are due by April 30, 2027, with payments in June, September, December and March, and the first payment must arrive by July 31.

faqs.q: Does Pasco County homestead carry over to the buyer when I sell?
faqs.a: No. The exemption belongs to the owner who lives there. The buyer must apply by March 1, and the sale resets the assessed value to just value on the next January 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pasco County house with delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the delinquent tax, including any certificate redemption costs, out of your sale proceeds before the deed passes. Ask the Tax Collector for the payoff figure at 352-521-4338, prompt 3.
